questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests binding of feature flags to artifact provenance and touches CI, runtime, and security controls across tenants.

## Key Concepts
- cosign signing and repo public keys
- SBOMs (CycloneDX)
- central provenance store and attestations
- manifest digest binding to provenance
- Kyverno admission policy

## Code Example
```yaml
name: Sign-and-attest
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
jobs:
  build-and-sign:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build image
        run: docker build -t my-registry/svc:$GITHUB_SHA .
      - name: cosign sign
        run: cosign sign --key cosign.pub my-registry/svc:$GITHUB_SHA
      - name: generate SBOM
        run: cyclonedx-bom -o bom.xml my-registry/svc:$GITHUB_SHA
      - name: upload SBOM
        run: curl -X POST -F file=@bom.xml https://provenance-store.local/upload
``` 

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test cross-tenant consistency?
- How would you rotate keys without breaking in-flight deploys?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to enforce cross-cloud data provenance and model lineage for ML workloads; ensures reproducibility and auditing of deployments.

## Key Concepts
- Policy-as-code with Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper
- Image digests, internal registries, provenance annotations
- MLflow tracking integration and run_id propagation
- Local and CI validation strategies

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-ml-provenance
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Fail
  rules:
  - name: require-provenance-annotations
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
    validate:
      message: 'Missing provenance annotations: model_version, dataset_hash, training_run_id'
      pattern:
        metadata:
          annotations:
            model_version: '*'
            dataset_hash: '*'
            training_run_id: '*'
  - name: require-image-digest
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
    validate:
      message: 'Container image must include a digest'
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - image: '*@*'
```

```yaml
# Failing Deployment (no provenance)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ml-inference-fail
  annotations:
    model_version: v1
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ml
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: predictor
        image: registry.internal/ml/predictor:latest
```

```yaml
# Passing Deployment (with provenance and digest)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ml-inference-pass
  annotations:
    model_version: v1.2.3
    dataset_hash: sha256:abcdef1234567890
    training_run_id: tr-789
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ml
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: predictor
        image: registry.internal/ml/predictor@sha256:12345abcdef
```

- conftest with YAML schemas for Kubernetes objects

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of identity-based runtime access control in Kubernetes, integrating SPIRE, OPA Gatekeeper, and admission/mutating webhooks for auditing. It also evaluates plan for cross-cloud (Snowflake/IBM) data workloads and secure Spark job execution.

## Key Concepts
- SPIRE workload identity and attestation
- OPA Gatekeeper constraint templates and validation hooks
- Kubernetes RBAC and API access control
- Mutating webhook for audit sidecars
- Validation strategy with compliant vs noncompliant pods

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (example): OPA-based API access gate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sapiaiaccess
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sAPIAccess
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |-
      package k8sapiaiaccess
      violate["API access denied: identity not whitelisted"] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        identity := input.review.object.metadata.annotations["spire.identity"]
        not identity_in_allowlist(identity)
      }
      
      # allowlisted identities (simplified)
      identity_in_allowlist(id) {
        id == "spiffe://cluster.local/ns/default/sa/spark-sa"
      }
```

```yaml
# Compliant Pod (SPIRE-identity annotated)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-spark
  annotations:
    spire.identity: "spiffe://cluster.local/ns/default/sa/spark-sa"
spec:
  serviceAccountName: spark-sa
  containers:
  - name: spark
    image: myrepo/spark:latest
```

```yaml
# Noncompliant Pod (no SPIRE identity)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: noncompliant-spark
spec:
  containers:
  - name: spark
    image: myrepo/spark:latest
```

## Validation Plan
- Deploy constraint template and constraint; attempt compliant pod deployment; verify admission allows and audit sidecar is injected. 
- Deploy noncompliant pod; confirm admission denies with clear event reason. 
- Run a Spark job and inspect API calls logged by the auditing sidecar for traceability.

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design runtime, policy-driven security for multi-tenant clusters, including per-tenant exceptions, scalable policy storage, and practical CI validation.

## Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Rego enforcement
- Runtime security: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, hostPath, privileged, SETUID checks
- Central PolicyStore for per-tenant overrides
- CI validation: dry-run, Gatekeeper evaluation, and manifest validation

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: runtimepolicy
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: RuntimePolicy
        listKind: RuntimePolicyList
        plural: runtimepolicies
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package runtimepolicy
      violation[{"msg": msg}]
      {
        input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.runAsNonRoot != true
        msg := "container must run as non-root"
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}]
      {
        any_cont := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
        not any_cont.securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem
        msg := "container must have readOnlyRootFilesystem: true"
      }
      # Additional rules for hostPath, privileged, and SETUID would follow similarly
```

```yaml
# Constraint (example)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: RuntimePolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-runtime-policy
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
      - apiGroups: ["apps"]
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    namespaces: ["tenant-a-*"]
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you manage updates to PolicyStore and revoke exceptions?
- How would you measure policy evaluation latency at scale?
